name: 993 K16 compressor wheel, F0 AlSi10Mg LPBF concept
description: Independent concept of an AlSi10Mg compressor wheel with six main blades and six straight splitters. Only the inducer/exducer diameters, the 6+6 count and the supplier part numbers are published; the hub, the bore and all aerodynamic surfaces remain F0 hypotheses.

classification.intended_use: CAD, DfAM, continuity, compressor thermodynamics, rotating disk, blade tension, expansion, imbalance and energy screening; no manufacturing, rotation, installation or start-up authorized

provenance.record_license: All rights reserved (see LICENSE) for the concept, the script and the calculations; no Porsche/BorgWarner/supplier photograph, surface or commercial geometry redistributed

sources.title: Invasion Auto Products - declared internal data of the right-hand 993 Turbo K16
sources.notes: Declares wheel 53241232006, 40.6 mm inducer, 60.5 mm exducer and 6+6 blades for the right-hand K16 53169886735. No profile, tolerance, material or process. See SRC-INVASIONAUTOPRODUCTS-993-K16-INTERNAL-DATA.

sources.title: PorscheFanatics - context of 993 turbochargers
sources.notes: Confirms the twin-turbo system and the upgrade wheel market, but no LPBF K16 wheel and no geometry. See SRC-PORSCHEFANATICS-993-K16-COMPRESSOR-WHEEL-CANDIDATE.

sources.title: EOS Aluminium AlSi10Mg
sources.notes: Provides generic LPBF properties that depend on machine, orientation and treatment; no rotor qualification. See SRC-EOS-ALSI10MG-CURRENT-PAGE.

sources.title: TurboMaster - principles for reading a compressor map
sources.notes: Methodological reference only for corrected flow, pressure ratio, efficiency, surge and choke; no usable K16 map. See SRC-TURBOMAP-COMPRESSOR-MAP-METHODOLOGY.

sources.title: elferclassic - 993 Turbo technical data
sources.notes: Documents 3.6 liters; the 5,750 rpm speed, volumetric filling, flow and the whole compressor operating point are synthetic. See SRC-ELFERCLASSIC-993-TURBO-TECHNICAL-DATA.

material.grade: EOS AlSi10Mg, screening; alloy and process of the BorgWarner wheel not published
material.standard: DIN EN 1706 / ASTM F3318 for the powder and a program-specific rotor specification to be contracted

post_processing: orientation, blade supports and recoater strategy to be qualified
stress relief and heat treatment qualified for machine, parameters and rotor fatigue
HIP to be decided on defects, toughness and overspeed results
machining of the bore, back face, nose, faces and balancing datums
deburring and controlled aerodynamic finishing of each blade and fillet
individual balancing then rotor-assembly balancing, spin proof and contained overspeed
supplier_requirements: traceable powder, machine, parameters, orientation, lot and recycling
oriented coupons with tensile, HCF, toughness, crack growth and defects at temperature
distortion simulation and witnesses for blades, exducer, hub and bore
full CT before and after machining, defect criteria by zone, and metallography
metrology of profiles, thicknesses, fillets, bore, runouts and polar mass
high-speed balancing, spin proof, overspeed, burst and containment validation before turbo rig testing

titanium.galvanic_isolation: Qualify the AlSi10Mg interface with shaft, nut, backplate and condensate, as well as fretting, corrosion and differential expansion.

known_limits: Only the 40.6 mm, 60.5 mm, six main blades, six splitters and the part numbers come from the supplier page.
The 3 mm disk, 18 mm height, 6 mm bore, the hub and all the straight blades are synthetic.
The 32.70 g STEP is not comparable to a real K16 wheel; the 4.22 ratio uses a theoretical envelope cylinder, not an industrial blank.
The 103,464 rpm speed is derived from Mach 0.9 at 330 K, not measured on the K16.
The 3.6 l, 5,750 rpm, VE 0.95, PR 1.8 and 0.72 efficiency point is a regression case without a compressor map.
The main blade reaches 390.9 MPa in the overspeed screen, a ratio of 0.63 against the ambient limit: the F0 design fails.
The disk/blade models ignore real shape, fillets, bore, preload, defects, HCF, rotor dynamics, contact and containment.
The EOS values are ambient comparisons, not allowables for a printed AlSi10Mg rotor.
The STEP proves only a readable twelve-blade BREP; it is authorized neither for manufacturing, nor for rotation, nor for a turbo or an engine.
